title: Oats upma
summary: Oats cooked savoury instead of sweet, with a South Indian tempering. Ten minutes and it does not taste remotely like porridge.

ingredients.note: Dry roast them first - it stops the whole thing turning to glue.

steps: Dry roast the oats in the pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until they smell nutty. Tip them out and set aside.
Same pan, heat the oil. Splutter the mustard seeds, then add urad dal and peanuts and take them to light gold.
Curry leaves and asafoetida in - stand back, they spit. Then onion, chilli and ginger for 3 minutes.
Carrot, peas, turmeric and salt. Cook 3-4 minutes until the carrot loses its rawness.
Pour in the hot water and bring to a boil.
Add the roasted oats all at once, stir hard for 30 seconds, then cover and turn the heat right down for 3 minutes.
Uncover, fluff with a fork, finish with lemon and coriander.
tips: Hot water, not cold - cold water makes it gummy.
1:1.5 oats to water is the ratio. More than that and you get porridge.
Two eggs scrambled in at the end, or a handful of roasted peanuts, brings it up to a real protein number.
health_notes: Beta-glucan fibre from oats without the sugar that usually comes with them. Use oil rather than ghee to keep it vegan.

source.adapted: Rava upma method with oats swapped in for semolina, which roughly doubles the fibre.
